data.q: Which type in the sync package provides a mutual exclusion lock?
data.e: sync.Mutex is the standard mutual exclusion lock. sync.RWMutex is a reader/writer mutex.

data.q: What happens if you call Lock() on an already locked sync.Mutex in the same goroutine?
data.e: A standard sync.Mutex is not re-entrant. Locking it twice from the same goroutine causes a deadlock.

data.q: Which method should be used to unlock a sync.Mutex?
data.e: The method to release a mutex lock is Unlock(). It is a runtime error to unlock an unlocked mutex.

data.q: What is the primary difference between sync.Mutex and sync.RWMutex?
o: RWMutex is faster for all operations
RWMutex allows multiple readers or a single writer
data.e: sync.RWMutex allows multiple goroutines to hold a read lock (RLock) simultaneously, but only one to hold a write lock (Lock). sync.Mutex allows only one holder total.

data.q: Which WaitGroup method increments the counter?
data.e: Add(delta int) increments the counter by delta (usually 1). Done() decrements it. Wait() blocks until the counter is zero.

data.q: What is the correct pattern to use sync.WaitGroup with a goroutine?
data.e: Add(1) must be called before the goroutine starts to avoid a race condition where Wait() returns before Add is called. defer wg.Done() ensures the counter decrements even on panic.

o: A function runs exactly once, regardless of how many times Do is called
A function runs once per goroutine
A function runs at most once, but may not run if Do is not called
data.e: sync.Once guarantees the function passed to Do(f) executes exactly once (the first time Do is called). If Do is never called, f never runs.

data.q: If the function passed to sync.Once.Do panics, what happens on subsequent calls to Do?
o: Do returns immediately without running the function
data.e: If the function panics, sync.Once considers it 'executed'. Subsequent calls to Do do nothing (the function is not re-run, and the panic is not re-raised).

data.q: Which type is a concurrent-safe map implementation in the sync package?
data.e: sync.Map is optimized for two common use cases: entry written once but read many times, and multiple goroutines reading/writing disjoint keysets.

o: Updates the value only if key exists
Sets the value for a key
data.e: Store sets the value for a key. Load retrieves. LoadOrStore retrieves or sets if missing. Delete removes.

data.q: What is the purpose of sync.Pool?
o: To manage a pool of goroutines
To cache allocated but unused objects to reduce GC pressure
To synchronize access to a shared resource
To limit the number of concurrent operations
data.e: sync.Pool is a temporary object cache. It helps reduce garbage collection pressure by reusing allocated memory (e.g., byte slices, structs).

data.q: When an object is retrieved from sync.Pool via Get(), what happens if the pool is empty?
o: It blocks until an object is Put back
It calls the New function (if set) to create one
data.e: If the pool is empty and a New function was provided during initialization, Get() calls New to create a new object. Otherwise, it returns nil.

data.q: Which type provides a condition variable for goroutine signaling?
data.e: sync.Cond implements a condition variable, allowing goroutines to wait for a condition (Wait) and be notified (Signal/Broadcast).

data.q: What must be held when calling cond.Wait()?
data.e: cond.Wait() atomically unlocks cond.L and suspends the goroutine. Upon resume, it re-locks cond.L before returning. The caller must hold cond.L before calling Wait.

data.q: What is the difference between cond.Signal() and cond.Broadcast()?
o: Signal wakes all waiters; Broadcast wakes one
Signal wakes one waiter; Broadcast wakes all waiters
Signal is for Mutex; Broadcast is for RWMutex
data.e: Signal wakes a single goroutine waiting on the condition. Broadcast wakes all goroutines waiting on the condition.

data.q: Is it safe to copy a sync.Mutex by value (e.g., passing struct containing it by value)?
o: Yes, it creates a new independent lock
No, it copies the internal state leading to undefined behavior
data.e: sync.Mutex (and other sync types) must not be copied. They contain internal state (like semaphores) that must not be duplicated. Always pass pointers to structs containing mutexes.

data.q: Which of the following is NOT a method on sync.WaitGroup?
data.e: sync.WaitGroup has Add, Done, and Wait. It does not have a Reset method; a WaitGroup cannot be reused after Wait returns unless the counter is zero and no new Adds happen concurrently (effectively a new zero-value WaitGroup should be used).
